title: Context railway and telemetry escrow for batch SDKs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight "context railway" abstraction and a "telemetry escrow" mechanism for Redwood SDKs that commonly run in batch/worker environments (e.g., job queues, map-reduce style workers, and long-running micro-batch processors). Goal: ensure robust, low-overhead trace/span propagation and reliable emission of telemetry when work is handed off between processes or when partial spans need to survive transient failures or preemption.
background: Current SDK context propagation focuses on synchronous request/response flows and streaming handlers. We frequently see gaps for background/batch workloads: spans that never finish because a worker is preempted, lost correlations when serialized payloads round-trip through queues, and excessive instrumentation complexity in customer code to checkpoint trace state. This ticket designs and implements a runtime-friendly pattern to reduce lost telemetry while keeping per-request overhead minimal.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exports a ContextRailway API (Node/Python/Go) with a 1-line handoff helper for enqueue/dequeue semantics.
Telemetry escrow: SDKs buffer partial spans and use a cluster-backed (or local-file fallback) escrow identifier to retry/emit after restart.
Lease tokens ensure idempotent span emission and prevent duplicate root spans in retries.
End-to-end tests that simulate worker preemption, queue requeue, and multi-worker handoff show >99.9% correlation preservation vs baseline (manual instrumentation) in test harness.
Feature gated and rollout plan documented; observability dashboards show no >3x increase in trace volume due to duplicate spans during canary.
Documentation and code examples added to SDK quickstarts and Console troubleshooting guide.
design_decisions: Use an explicit lightweight envelope for context (trace_id, span_id_hint, lease_nonce, sampling_hint, and optional kv-checksum) to avoid coupling to full tracing SDK internals.

Telemetry escrow default is in-process circular buffer with optional S3/Blob+index for very large payloads; cluster-backed escrow implemented as a best-effort enhancement for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Lease tokens are short-lived (default 5 minutes) and signed by the SDK to allow idempotent flushes; choice favors at-most-once emission semantics with detection for duplicates rather than exactly-once complexity.
We will not change existing OTLP payload formats — the railway operates as an SDK-level helper that synthesizes proper spans on flush.
Sampling hints flow through the envelope so the runtime can decide to preserve or retroactively sample partial traces.
implementation_notes: Add ContextRailway core in each SDK: startRailway(), attachToEnvelope(), handoffForEnqueue(), resumeFromEnvelope().
Implement escrow manager with pluggable backends: memory (default), local fs (node/python), and remote index (redis/blob) for Dedicated customers.
Create LeaseToken format: base64(payload|expiry|nonce|signature). Use existing KMS sig keys where available; fall back to ephemeral HMAC in hosted mode.
Instrumentation: provide a shallow wrapper that converts in-flight spans to 'partial-span' records and stores a canonical root hint in the envelope.
Add integration tests simulating: immediate worker shutdown, delayed dequeue, cross-language enqueue/dequeue (Node->Python), and high throughput to validate buffer sizing heuristics.
Console/Runtime hooks: emit telemetry when escrow size exceeds thresholds and expose per-railway metrics (escrow_count, escrow_flush_failures, lease_reissues).
progress_updates: 2026-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Observability, SDK, and Runtime teams. Agreed on envelope schema and basic API shape (notes in Confluence: /obs/context-railway-2026).
2026-02-21: Prototype implemented in node-sdk with memory escrow and simple lease token; local integration test passes for enqueue/handoff flow. PR: github.com/redwood/sdk-node/pull/2123
2026-02-28: Design review with Security & Privacy; approved HMAC fallback plan and KMS signing for Dedicated. Raised question about retention policy for escrowed telemetry (see review feedback).
2026-03-03: Python SDK port started; added cross-language envelope test harness. Draft RFC posted to teams/observability mailing list.
2026-03-07: Load test run against staging queue: observed 1.8% increase in trace events due to partial-span markers; added dedupe heuristics (lease nonce check) to reduce duplicates.
2026-03-10: Implementation PR opened for Node + test harness: github.com/redwood/sdk-node/pull/2189. Migration doc stub created: docs/redwood/context-railway.md
review_feedback: Security: require KMS-signed lease tokens for Dedicated customers; hosted tenants can use ephemeral signatures but must rotate keys hourly.
Privacy: limit escrow retention to 24 hours by default and add customer-configurable retention in Private deployments.
SDK: prefer smallest possible envelope; avoid carrying large KV caches inside the envelope to prevent queue bloat.
Observability: add a dashboard tile for 'railway orphan rate' (escrow items not flushed within lease expiry).
risks: Potential for duplicate spans if leases are reissued aggressively; mitigated by nonce/signature dedupe on ingest path.
Increased trace volume during rollout leading to quota spikes; rollout must be gated with feature flags and per-customer rate controls.
Cross-language envelope version skew causing lost correlations; enforce a minor-version compatibility matrix in SDKs and runtime.
rollout_plan: Feature flag default OFF for all tenants.
Internal canary: enable for 3 internal services with low QPS, monitor orphan rate and trace volume for 72h.
Gradual enablement for Hosted customers by opt-in; Dedicated/Private customers can enable via console or config with KMS key binding.
Revert criteria: orphan_rate > 0.1% for 24h OR trace volume > 2x baseline sustained for 6h.
